title: Converge a VCF Operations maintenance schedule idempotently
prompt: Implement the exported Set-VcfOpsMaintenanceWindow function in src/VcfOps.MaintenanceWindow/VcfOps.MaintenanceWindow.psm1. The environment provides the genuine `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops` PowerCLI module version 13.5.0.25380678. Before implementing, research the maintenance-schedule operations and their generated VMware VCF PowerCLI 9.1 bindings in official VMware sources. Cite the sources consulted in the final answer; drive VCF Operations through Initialize-VcfOpsschedule, Initialize-VcfOpsmaintenanceschedule, Invoke-VcfOpsGetMaintenanceSchedules, Invoke-VcfOpsCreateMaintenanceSchedules, and Invoke-VcfOpsUpdateMaintenanceSchedules rather than a direct HTTP client. The fleet maintenance orchestrator restarts an interrupted plan from the top, so calling this function again with the same arguments must converge instead of leaving a second schedule behind. A schedule key is unique across the system and createMaintenanceSchedules answers HTTP 422 when the key is already taken, so read the schedule that currently holds Key before mutating anything. When no schedule holds the key, create it and let the server assign the identifier: the create request must not preassign an id. When a schedule holds the key and already matches the requested definition, send no write request at all. When it holds the key but the stored definition differs, update it in place carrying the identifier the server already assigned. Map DurationMinutes onto the schedule duration field. Support ONCE, DAILY, and WEEKLY schedules. ONCE needs only the four required schedule fields. DAILY requires Recurrence and at least one of ExpirationDate or ExpireRuns, and must not include DaysOfTheWeek. WEEKLY requires Recurrence, a nonempty DaysOfTheWeek value, and at least one of ExpirationDate or ExpireRuns. Reject unsupported types and invalid field combinations before issuing any SDK request. The service may add startDate to a returned schedule; treat that as server-owned state and never emit startDate in a create or update request. Only parameters the caller actually bound may reach the wire: unbound optional fields must be omitted from the JSON body entirely rather than sent as null, an empty string, an empty array, or a zero, and dayOfTheMonth, daysOfTheMonth, month, months, startDate, and weeksOfTheMonth must never be emitted. Treat an optional field the caller did not bind as drift when the stored schedule has a value for it, and compare DaysOfTheWeek as a set so that reordering the days is not a change. Return a PSCustomObject carrying Key, Id, and Action, where Action is Created, Updated, or Unchanged and Id is the server-assigned schedule identifier in all three cases. Keep the existing public function signature and module manifest compatible. Do not use Invoke-RestMethod, Invoke-WebRequest, WebClient, HttpClient, curl, or another direct HTTP client, and do not vendor, replace, or intercept the VMware prerequisite. Run `python3 -B tests/verify.py`. Verification checks use of the generated SDK bindings, convergence across repeated calls, exact request shapes, omission semantics, drift handling, and the Created/Updated/Unchanged result.
